title: Gardenio — Formula Step Dispatcher
description: Observability for the formula step-role dispatcher (gardenio/controller/internal/bridge/formula_step_dispatch.go, task ka-0000004839). The dispatcher spawns a role-matched agent when a formula step's blocking deps clear. It exists to prevent SILENT loss of a handoff (FSM-472), so its own operation must be visible: this dashboard answers 'did it spawn anything today?' (top row) and 'if not, why not?' (decline breakdown). Metrics scraped from trigger-engine :9092. Metric refs: gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_spawned_total, gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_declined_total. A further row answers 'how long did a ready step WAIT?' from gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_latency_seconds (task ka-0000006705): the readiness -> spawn interval as a real histogram, replacing the quantile_over_time proxy over the pending gauge. Metric refs: gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_latency_seconds, gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_latency_unmeasured_total.

options.content: **Formula step dispatch** — the spawn path from a gardener's formula step to a live agent. `spawned` and `declined` are the two terminal outcomes of every dispatch attempt: a decline is the engine refusing (cooldown, capacity, self-block), an **error-class** decline is trouble. The reconcile stat cross-checks the counter against `dispatched_by` beads — the two must agree, or one of the two is lying.

panels.title: Did it spawn anything? (the loss-prevention headline)
Agents spawned (window)
panels.description: sum(increase(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_spawned_total[$__range])) — total role-matched agents the dispatcher minted over the dashboard time range. THE loss-prevention headline: if this reads 0 while the decline counter below is climbing, every candidate is declining — the G1 signature (all opt-in steps unreachable). The raw counter lives on the SHORT-LIVED trigger-engine pod, so an INSTANT count(spawned_total) reads 0 between spawns — always use increase() over a window, never the instantaneous series. A 0 here means the dispatcher was idle or every candidate declined in-window, NOT a dead emitter or scrape outage (declined_total shares this process + :9092 and is live). As of 2026-08-14 the emitter is live and correct (recordSpawn on the spawn-success branch, gardenio/controller/internal/bridge/formula_step_dispatch.go). It RECONCILES (advice ka-0000005924) with derivation B, count(beads with dispatched_by=formula-step-dispatcher): A == B == 5 over 30d (increase[7d]=3), so a flat window is a real idle/all-declined state, not a dead counter. The prior opt-in-gap framing (bug ka-0000007851) is obsolete: 8 formulas now declare suggest_new_agent steps and the counter emits (bug ka-0000000749). Empty-branch liveness: the `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `count(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_declined_total) > 0` — the decline counter registered by the same dispatcher in the same process — so a green 0 is an evidenced idle/all-declined window, and a genuinely dark dispatcher leaves the panel empty instead.

defaults.noValue: exporter dark — the trigger-engine dispatcher is not reporting, so this window's spawn count is unknown rather than 0

panels.title: Declines (window)
panels.description: sum(increase(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_declined_total[$__range])) — total candidate steps NOT dispatched over the range. A large number is not itself bad (most declines are the correct 'not opted in' / 'still blocked' / dedup outcomes); read it against the spawn count and the reason breakdown below.

panels.title: Reconcile: spawns (window) vs dispatched_by beads
panels.description:
sum(increase(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_spawned_total[$__range])) — derivation A of 'agents the dispatcher minted', over the SAME window you reconcile against derivation B. Advice ka-0000005924 wants the quantity measured two independent ways so the derivations must agree. Derivation B is the durable bead count (dispatch() stamps dispatched_by=formula-step-dispatcher on exactly the steps it spawned for; rolled back on spawn failure, so a bead carries it iff a spawn succeeded). Prometheus cannot query the beads daemon, so run B yourself over the same window and confirm equality:
  kd count --all-types --all-projects -f dispatched_by=formula-step-dispatcher --created-after <window-start>
As of 2026-08-14 A == B == 5. A persistent gap is a bug in one derivation. The raw counter lives on the SHORT-LIVED trigger-engine pod, so an INSTANT count(spawned_total) reads 0 between spawns — always use increase() over a window, never the instantaneous series. Full procedure: gardenio/docs/formula-step-dispatch-observability.md. Empty-branch liveness: the `or vector(0)` fallback is gated on `count(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_declined_total) > 0` — the decline counter registered by the same dispatcher in the same process — so a green 0 is an evidenced idle/all-declined window, and a genuinely dark dispatcher leaves the panel empty instead.

panels.title: Spawns over time, by role
panels.description: sum by (role) (increase(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_spawned_total[1h])). 'Did the monorepo-fix lane spawn anything?' — a lane you expect active that stays flat-zero across a wide range is the alertable signal. Spawns are BURSTY and infrequent (a handful per week), so widen the dashboard range to see them; each spawn renders as a ~1h-wide unit pulse. As of 2026-08-14 the emitter is live and correct (recordSpawn on the spawn-success branch, gardenio/controller/internal/bridge/formula_step_dispatch.go). It RECONCILES (advice ka-0000005924) with derivation B, count(beads with dispatched_by=formula-step-dispatcher): A == B == 5 over 30d (increase[7d]=3), so a flat window is a real idle/all-declined state, not a dead counter. The prior opt-in-gap framing (bug ka-0000007851) is obsolete: 8 formulas now declare suggest_new_agent steps and the counter emits (bug ka-0000000749). An empty window means no opted-in step was dispatched then, not a dead emitter (the by-reason decline panels share this process and are live).

defaults.noValue: Nothing dispatched in the selected window. Dispatches are bursty and rare — widen the range. Cross-check the decline panels below: if they are populated, the dispatcher is reporting and this window is genuinely idle.

panels.title: Spawns over time, by formula
panels.description: sum by (formula) (increase(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_spawned_total[1h])). Which formulas' opt-in (suggest_new_agent) steps actually reach a dispatched agent. A formula that declares opt-in steps but never appears here is the G1 gap surfaced as data. As of 2026-08-14 formula ka-0000006208 (monorepo-fix lane) is the active source and 8 formulas now declare opt-in steps; the emitter reconciles with the dispatched_by bead count (A == B == 5). Spawns are bursty — widen the range to see them; empty = feature not exercised in-window, not a broken board.

defaults.noValue: Nothing dispatched in the selected window. Dispatches are bursty and rare — widen the range. Cross-check the decline panels below: if they are populated, the dispatcher is reporting and this window is genuinely idle.

panels.title: Declines per hour, by reason
panels.description: sum by (reason) (increase(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_declined_total[1h])). The 'why not?' answer. Benign-and-expected reasons: not_opted_in (most formulas keep one driver), still_blocked (sibling deps not all closed yet), already_dispatched_process / already_stamped / already_assigned (idempotency working). Reasons that warrant a look when sustained: guard_refused (fleet spawn budget exhausted), spawn_failed (SpawnAgent erroring), stamp_failed / hydrate_failed / listdeps_failed / block_check_failed (daemon trouble), unknown (a caller bug — should never appear).

panels.title: Decline reasons (window share)
panels.description: topk share of declines by reason over the range — the quick 'what is the dispatcher mostly declining on?' read. A window dominated by not_opted_in/still_blocked is healthy; a growing wedge of spawn_failed/guard_refused/*_failed/unknown is the thing to chase.

panels.title: Error-class declines only (daemon / spawn trouble)
panels.description: The subset of declines that are NOT the expected opt-in/idempotency/blocked outcomes: guard_refused, spawn_failed, stamp_failed, hydrate_failed, listdeps_failed, block_check_failed, unknown. These are the ones that mean a step that SHOULD have dispatched didn't. Sustained non-zero here is worth an operator's attention — an eligible handoff is being dropped for an infrastructural reason.

panels.title: How long did a ready step wait? (dispatch latency)
Dispatch latency percentiles (p50 / p95 / p99), by path
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.50|0.95|0.99, sum by (le, path) (increase(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_latency_seconds_bucket[$__range]))) — how long a formula step sat WORKABLE before its agent existed. The interval is measured from the daemon-side max(closed_at) over the step's blocking deps (the instant it became dispatchable) to the instant SpawnAgent returned, and it is observed ONLY on the spawn-success branch, so a declined or failed dispatch never contributes a sample (task ka-0000006705, gardenio/controller/internal/bridge/formula_step_dispatch.go). Read the two paths separately — they are different systems: path=event is the SSE-driven hot path and should be sub-second to seconds; path=backfill is the 2-minute BackfillReadySteps sweep recovering a step the event path missed, and is LEGITIMATELY minutes to hours. A rising event-path p95 is the actionable signal; backfill p95 tells you how long the safety net took, and any backfill traffic at all means the hot path dropped something. Measured from the readiness instant, not from event ingress, deliberately: a readiness signal that reached nobody is exactly the FSM-472 silent-loss class this dispatcher exists to prevent, and an ingress-anchored clock would hide it. RARE-EVENT CAVEAT: at a handful of dispatches per week these percentiles step rather than curve, and a window holding one sample puts p50 == p95 == p99 in that sample's bucket. Read the windowed-mean panel and the bucket heatmap below alongside them before concluding a percentile moved. Bucket resolution is 0.25s–1h, so a healthy sub-second dispatch and an hour-long sweep rescue both land in a real bucket rather than the +Inf overflow. NOT the same clock as the prewarm-assign panel above: that one measures the NEXT segment (gardenio_prewarmed_assign_duration_seconds — dispatch → warm seat), this one measures the segment BEFORE it (ready → dispatch). Add them for the end-to-end wait; a slow total is attributable to exactly one of the two.

defaults.noValue: No latency samples in this window. A dispatch is a handful-per-week event, so widen the range first. If the spawn headline above shows dispatches in the SAME window while this stays empty, the spawns were unmeasurable rather than fast — read the unmeasured-by-reason panel, not this one.

panels.title: Dispatch latency p95 (window, both paths)
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (increase(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_latency_seconds_bucket[$__range]))) — the one-number headline for 'is the dispatcher slow right now?', pooled across both paths so a single tile answers it. Pooled ON PURPOSE here and split on the panel to the left: pooling makes any backfill rescue in the window dominate the number, which is the correct alarm (a step that needed the sweep waited minutes), but it means a red tile should always be attributed on the per-path panel before acting. Colour thresholds: <60s healthy, 60s slower than the event path should ever be, 300s past the sweep interval so the event path likely missed the step, 1800s the FSM-472 silent-loss shape the sweep rescued. No `or vector(0)` fallback by design (grounded-zero sweep, bug ka-0000006531): a fabricated 0 here would read as an instant dispatch and is indistinguishable from a real one, so an empty window renders the noValue text instead.

defaults.noValue: No latency samples in this window. A dispatch is a handful-per-week event, so widen the range first. If the spawn headline above shows dispatches in the SAME window while this stays empty, the spawns were unmeasurable rather than fast — read the unmeasured-by-reason panel, not this one.

panels.title: Windowed mean dispatch latency, by path (the robust companion)
panels.description: sum by (path) (increase(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_latency_seconds_sum[$__range])) / sum by (path) (increase(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_latency_seconds_count[$__range])) — the arithmetic mean over the window, and the panel to trust when the percentiles above look jumpy. It needs no bucket interpolation, so a single-sample window reports that sample exactly instead of reporting a bucket edge. Read it as the second, independently-derived view of the same quantity the percentile panel estimates (advice ka-0000005924): the two must stay in the same neighbourhood, and a mean far ABOVE p95 means one enormous outlier — usually a backfill rescue — is carrying the window. This is the honest version of the metric the richness lane could only approximate: before this histogram existed the board had to proxy dispatch delay with quantile_over_time over the pending gauge, which measures queue depth over time rather than any individual step's wait (task ka-0000006705).

defaults.noValue: No latency samples in this window. A dispatch is a handful-per-week event, so widen the range first. If the spawn headline above shows dispatches in the SAME window while this stays empty, the spawns were unmeasurable rather than fast — read the unmeasured-by-reason panel, not this one.

panels.title: Dispatch latency distribution (bucket heatmap)
panels.description: sum by (le) (increase(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_latency_seconds_bucket[$__interval])) rendered as a pre-bucketed heatmap — the actual SHAPE of the distribution, which no percentile can show: whether dispatches cluster in one band or are genuinely bimodal (the expected healthy shape is exactly that — a sub-second event-path cluster plus a sparse minutes-to-hours backfill tail). Uses $__interval rather than $__range because a heatmap needs one column per time step; at a handful of dispatches per week most columns are legitimately EMPTY and each dispatch renders as an isolated cell at its bucket. That sparsity is the data, not a broken panel — use the percentile and mean panels for the trend and this one to ask 'which bucket do dispatches actually land in?'.

defaults.noValue: No gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_latency_seconds_bucket samples in this range — no formula step was dispatched in the window. Widen the range first: a handful of dispatches per week leaves most $__interval columns legitimately empty. A persistently blank heatmap across a range where the spawn headline shows dispatches means those spawns were unmeasurable — read the unmeasured-by-reason panel.

panels.title: Accounting: latency samples + unmeasured == spawns
panels.description: The built-in cross-check that makes the histogram's _count a trustworthy denominator instead of a silent undercount (advice ka-0000005924). Every SUCCESSFUL dispatch produces exactly one accounting entry — either a latency sample or an gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_latency_unmeasured_total increment — so samples + unmeasured must equal gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_spawned_total over any window. The 'accounted' series plots that sum directly: it should sit exactly on top of 'spawns'. A persistent gap is a bug in this instrumentation, not a fact about the dispatcher, and the unit test TestStepDispatchLatency_CountPlusUnmeasuredReconcilesWithSpawns pins the same invariant in code. Why an explicit unmeasured counter exists at all: some real dispatches have no readiness instant to measure from (a step with no blocking dep) or an unreadable one (a cleared blocker carrying neither closed_at nor updated_at). Skipping those silently would shrink _count with no trace; counting them by reason keeps a gap in the histogram attributable instead of mysterious. This panel renders as soon as the dispatcher is up even with zero dispatches, because the constructor seeds both histogram paths and all three unmeasured reasons with zero-valued children — the metric-name existence problem that made bug ka-0000003699 refindable three times. A seeded child contributes 0 to every bucket, so it publishes the series without fabricating a sample or moving a quantile.

defaults.noValue: Neither the latency families nor the spawn counter reported in this window — the trigger-engine dispatcher is dark, so the accounting is UNKNOWN rather than balanced. The constructor seeds both latency paths and all three unmeasured reasons, so a live dispatcher populates this panel even across a window with zero dispatches.

panels.title: Unmeasured dispatches, by reason (why a spawn has no latency)
panels.description:
sum by (reason) (increase(gardenio_formula_step_dispatch_latency_unmeasured_total[$__range])) — the attribution for every successful dispatch MISSING from the latency histogram. Read it whenever the spawn headline shows dispatches that the percentile panels do not. The reason enum is hard-bounded in code (an out-of-enum value is coerced rather than minting a new label), so this panel can never blow up cardinality:
• no_blocking_deps — the step had no blocking dep, so there is no 'became workable' instant to measure from. Structurally unmeasurable and entirely benign; expect the sweep to be the path.
• blocker_time_missing — a cleared blocker carried neither closed_at nor updated_at, so max(closed_at) would be a fiction. Also raised when only SOME blockers are readable, because the unreadable one may well have been the last to clear and a max over the readable subset would overstate the wait. A steady stream here means daemon timestamps are missing on closed beads — worth chasing.
• clock_skew — the readiness instant landed in the future relative to the dispatcher's clock. Dropped rather than clamped to 0, because a clamped 0 would read as a suspiciously fast dispatch and quietly corrupt every quantile above. Sustained non-zero means pod/daemon clock drift.
All three are seeded at zero on startup, so a flat zero line here is an evidenced 'every dispatch was measurable', not an absent series.

defaults.noValue: The unmeasured counters did not report in this window — the trigger-engine dispatcher is dark. All three reasons are seeded at zero on startup, so a live dispatcher shows a flat 0 line here rather than nothing.
